title: M/s J.P. Textiles v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pankaj Mithal and Prakash Padia, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; consumer relegated to CGRF/Ombudsman under clause 7.10.
headnote: A power-loom consumer’s dispute over subsidy under a Government Order and the correctness of a demand bill is for the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and, by appeal, the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The High Court declined writ interference and disposed of the petition with liberty to take that route.
facts: M/s J.P. Textiles, a power-loom consumer with a 3 H.P. connection, claimed subsidy under a Government Order dated 14 June 2006. The Executive Engineer, by order dated 15 March 2019, held that the subsidy applied only to power-loom connections up to 1 H.P. and that the petitioner’s 3 H.P. connection fell outside its purview. A bill dated 21 February 2019 was raised without subsidy. The consumer challenged that order and demand in writ proceedings before the Allahabad High Court.

holding_units.topic: CGRF/Ombudsman as alternative remedy for subsidy and billing disputes
holding_units.holding: Where a consumer disputes admissibility of subsidy under a Government Order and the correctness of a demand bill, the remedy is to approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and thereafter the Ombudsman by appeal under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not exercise discretionary writ jurisdiction in such a case.
